summary: LyricPay: token-queue saturation at edge gateway caused GPU pool backpressure, streaming stalls and P0 escalation
description: Issue summary: LyricPay experienced a production outage beginning ~2026-03-12 03:15 UTC where a sudden client retry storm combined with an intermittent DNS failover caused token-queue saturation on the edge gateway. Saturation prevented requests from being admitted into the serving pipeline which in turn pushed bursty load into a subset of GPU pools, triggering autoscaler backpressure, long-tail queuing, increased 5xx responses and streaming stalls for streaming-enabled sessions. Impact: complete request failures and truncated streams for ~40% of LyricPay traffic in us-east-1 for ~2 hours, degraded latency for remaining requests, and noticeable billing spike due to request retries and duplicate completions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1. Simulate transient DNS failover for edge gateway subdomain (client resolves to new IPs intermittently).
2. Replay high-concurrency client retries with identical session keys and streaming enabled (2000 rps sustained).
3. Observe token admission queues growing on edge gateway and reject rate increase to serving-runtime.
4. Verify autoscaler did not provision capacity quickly due to cooldown policy and detected backpressure propagated to GPU pools.
timeline: 2026-03-12 03:10 UTC — LyricPay monitoring alerted on increase in 5xx and stream truncation (customer alerted support).
2026-03-12 03:18 UTC — Support acknowledged, P0 declared, SRE and on-call routed to #inc-lyricpay channel.
2026-03-12 03:25 UTC — Investigations pointed to edge-gateway token admission queue growth; DNS flapping observed in client traces.
2026-03-12 03:40 UTC — Applied short-term mitigation: temporary per-customer adaptive throttling and increased edge gateway admission window to drain queues.
2026-03-12 04:05 UTC — Autoscaler parameters relaxed for LyricPay GPU pool; additional reserved nodes brought online (manual scale-up).
2026-03-12 05:30 UTC — Traffic normalized; streaming sessions resumed. Continued monitoring and gradual rollback of emergency limits.
2026-03-12 12:00 UTC — Customer call with LyricPay CS and engineering to review root cause and immediate mitigations.
logs: edge-gateway: token_admit_queue_size spiked to 48k (steady-state ~300) for lyricpay-customer-id
serving-runtime: gpool-us-east-1a queue-lengths exceeded 95th percentile, kernel thrash observed on redwood-7b-quant instances
autoscaler: cooldown prevented scale from +0 -> +8 nodes due to recent sync at 02:58 UTC
dns-resolver: multiple NXDOMAIN/TTL expiry events recorded from LyricPay CDN between 03:12-03:22 UTC
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Client-side retry/backoff misconfiguration combined with transient DNS flapping leading to synchronous replay of requests against a small pool of serving nodes.
Hypothesis 2: Edge gateway token admission has a degenerate path when admission queue exceeds threshold that results in rejecting instead of shedding gracefully — explored and reproduced in staging.

Findings: Reproduced admission-queue growth in staging when replaying LyricPay traces; autoscaler cooldown policy kept scale from reacting quickly enough to the burst profile. Edge gateway lacked customer-specific admission shaping which amplified the fan-in.
Impact quantification: Peak affected sessions ~42% of LyricPay traffic; estimated duplicate-completion billing exposure ~0.9% of daily spend for LyricPay (billing team notified).
comments: Aisha Khan (Support) — 2026-03-12: Customer reported streaming sessions truncated and saw increased errors. We escalated to SRE.
SRE On-call (Rita Patel) — 2026-03-12: Confirmed admission-queue spike and DNS anomalies. Initiating temporary per-customer throttling.
Marcelo Ruiz (Infra Eng) — 2026-03-12: Manually increased LyricPay GPU pool by 6 nodes, adjusted autoscaler cooldown to 60s for affected pool. Monitoring continues.
LyricPay Engineering (J. Moreno) — 2026-03-12: We changed client retry logic yesterday; cooperating to share logs and DNS trace. Appreciate the quick mitigation.
Support Lead (Ellen Park) — 2026-03-13: Preparing formal post-incident report and a credit proposal to customer; flagged for billing review.
resolution: Immediate: applied per-customer adaptive throttling, increased admission window, and manually scaled LyricPay GPU pool to absorb burst. Autoscaler cooldown temporarily reduced and a short-lived override allowed fast scale-up. Long-term: implemented customer-specific admission shaping, adjusted autoscaler heuristics for bursty retry storms, and added detection rules to alert on token-queue growth earlier. Billing: finance approved a one-time usage credit for LyricPay equal to the estimated duplicate-completion exposure.
postincident_followup: 1) Engineering: Deploy edge-gateway admission-shaping v1 (customer-scoped token caps) — owner: Marcelo Ruiz — due 2026-03-20.
2) SRE: Update autoscaler runbook and allow emergency override path for dedicated pools — owner: Rita Patel — due 2026-03-18.
3) Telemetry: Add token_admit_queue_size anomaly alert with 5m and 1m thresholds for P0 customers — owner: Observability team — due 2026-03-16.
4) Support/CS: Customer action plan and RCA call summary to be sent to LyricPay, include timeline and credit details — owner: Aisha Khan — due 2026-03-13.
5) Product: Consider public runbook snippets for client retry best-practices in dedicated docs — owner: Product Docs — due 2026-04-01.
